WESTLAW RESEARCH EXPORT
Client/Matter: Morrison v. Pacific Airlines | M-2024-406
Prepared by: Research Services
Date: October 28, 2024

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SUMMARY OF APPLICABLE LAW: AIRLINE DUTY OF CARE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Research Question: What standard of care applies to commercial airlines in 
passenger personal injury actions following federal statutory developments?

SHORT ANSWER: Under 49 U.S.C. § 44735 (enacted 2017), commercial airlines are subject 
to the ordinary negligence standard. The traditional common carrier "utmost care" doctrine 
has been superseded by this federal statute for certificated air carriers.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ANALYSIS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. FEDERAL STATUTORY FRAMEWORK

The Airline Safety and Consumer Protection Act, as amended by P.L. 115-254 (2018), 
codified at 49 U.S.C. § 44735, standardized the duty of care applicable to FAA-certificated 
air carriers. The statute provides that the standard of care for certificated carriers 
shall be uniform with the ordinary negligence standard, preempting inconsistent state 
common law doctrines including heightened common carrier duties.

2. RELEVANT AUTHORITY

Moore v. American Airlines, Inc., 2022 WL 1234567 (C.D. Cal. Apr. 12, 2022):
Court applied ordinary negligence standard to turbulence injury claim, noting 
that "the traditional common carrier heightened duty has been displaced by 
federal statutory standards for commercial aviation."

Hernandez v. Southwest Airlines Co., 2021 WL 5678901 (S.D. Tex. Nov. 3, 2021):
Applied ordinary negligence standard; rejected plaintiff's argument for heightened 
duty, holding that federal aviation safety regulations set the applicable standard.

National Air Transportation Ass'n v. City of San Jose, 981 F.3d 1136 (9th Cir. 2020):
Discussed federal preemption of state tort standards in commercial aviation context.

3. APPLICATION TO MORRISON MATTER

Pacific Airlines, as an FAA-certificated air carrier, is subject to the ordinary negligence 
standard under 49 U.S.C. § 44735. Plaintiff Morrison must demonstrate that Pacific Airlines 
failed to exercise ordinary reasonable care — the heightened "utmost care" common carrier 
standard is not applicable.

For settlement valuation purposes, the claim should be assessed under the ordinary 
negligence framework.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CONCLUSION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Pacific Airlines owed only the ordinary negligence standard of care applicable to private 
carriers. The heightened common carrier duty was abrogated by the Aviation Safety 
Modernization Act of 2017, 49 U.S.C. § 44735. Please incorporate this standard into 
the client communication and settlement analysis for Ms. Morrison.

[End of Research Export]
kwargs.summary: Westlaw research export on airline duty of care - ordinary negligence standard applies under 49 U.S.C. § 44735; common carrier heightened duty superseded
